dublinCore.dc:title: 119 HR 9989 IH: Candidate Investment Transparency and Ethics Act of 2026
dublinCore.dc:rights: Pursuant to Title 17 Section 105 of the United States Code, this file is not subject to copyright protection and is in the public domain.

action.action-desc: Mr. Mackenzie introduced the following bill; which was referred to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, and in addition to the Committee on House Administration, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned

form.official-title: To require candidates for Federal office to divest publicly traded securities or place such securities in a qualified blind trust upon filing for office, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Candidate Investment Transparency and Ethics Act of 2026 or the CITE Act of 2026.

paragraph.text: The term candidate means any individual who files a statement of candidacy or statement of organization with the Federal Election Commission or otherwise formally declares their intention to seek election to—

subparagraph.text: the Office of President or Vice President of the United States;
the United States House of Representatives.

paragraph.text: The term covered investment means any security issued by a publicly traded company, including—

subparagraph.text: bonds, debentures, or other debt instruments of a publicly traded issuer;
stock options, warrants, or convertible securities; and
exchange-traded funds and similar products that hold individual securities of publicly traded companies, except to the extent such funds qualify as exempt investments under paragraph (4).

paragraph.text: The term covered individual means a candidate and the spouse and dependent children of the candidate.
The term exempt investment means—

subparagraph.text: index funds or exchange-traded funds that track a broad market index, including the S&P 500, the Dow Jones Industrial Average, or a comparable index;
widely diversified exchange-traded funds, including sector-based or thematic exchange-traded funds;
United States Treasury securities, obligations of the United States Government, or obligations of State or local governments;
certificates of deposit, money market funds, and cash equivalents; and
interests in a defined benefit pension plan or similar retirement arrangement not subject to individual investment direction.

paragraph.text: The term filing date means the date on which a candidate files any document with the Federal Election Commission, a State election authority, or the Clerk of the House of Representatives or the Secretary of the Senate that formally initiates the candidacy.
The term qualified blind trust has the meaning given that term under section 13104(f)(3) of title 5, United States Code.
The term supervising ethics office means—

subparagraph.text: the Committee on Ethics of the House of Representatives, for candidates for the House of Representatives;
the Select Committee on Ethics of the Senate, for candidates for the Senate; and
the Office of Government Ethics, for candidates for President or Vice President.

section.header: Divestiture or blind trust requirement for candidates for federal office

subsection.text: Not later than 90 days after the filing date, each covered individual shall—

paragraph.text: divest all covered investments held by the covered individual; or
place all covered investments held by the covered individual into a qualified blind trust that meets the requirements of subsection (b).

subsection.text: A qualified blind trust established pursuant to subsection (a)(2) shall—

paragraph.text: be established and administered in accordance with the requirements of section 13104(f) of title 5, United States Code;
be managed by an independent trustee who is not a relative, business associate, or political affiliate of the covered individual;
prohibit the covered individual from having any knowledge of, or influence over, the investment decisions made by the trustee; and
prohibit any communication between the covered individual and the trustee regarding the assets or transactions within the trust, except as required by law or for tax purposes.

subsection.text: Not later than 90 days after the filing date, each covered individual shall file a written certification with the applicable supervising ethics office attesting that—

paragraph.text: the covered individual holds no covered investments other than exempt investments; or
all covered investments have been placed in a qualified blind trust in compliance with this section, including the name of the trustee and the financial institution administering the trust.

subsection.text: A covered individual shall make good faith efforts to ensure that the covered investments of a spouse or dependent child are divested or placed in a qualified blind trust pursuant to this section. If a spouse maintains legally independent finances and does not consent to such divestiture or placement, the candidate shall certify such fact to the supervising ethics office, which shall have authority to determine whether an exemption is warranted.

section.header: Prohibition on acquisition of covered investments during candidacy

subsection.text: During the period beginning on the filing date and ending on the date on which the covered individual is no longer a candidate or no longer holds or is seeking Federal office, a covered individual may not purchase or otherwise acquire any new covered investment.

paragraph.text: the receipt of a covered investment as part of a will, trust distribution, or similar inheritance, provided that such investment is divested or placed in a qualified blind trust within 90 days of receipt; and
purchases made within a qualified blind trust established pursuant to section 3.

subsection.text: Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Committee on Ethics of the House of Representatives, the Select Committee on Ethics of the Senate, and the Office of Government Ethics shall each issue regulations to carry out this Act with respect to candidates under their respective jurisdiction.
The regulations issued under subsection (a) shall include—

paragraph.text: procedures for filing and reviewing certifications under section 3(c);
standards for determining whether a trust qualifies as a qualified blind trust for purposes of this Act; and
a process for covered individuals to request a hardship waiver, which may be granted only in extraordinary circumstances and shall be made publicly available.

subsection.text: Nothing in this Act shall be construed to limit the application of the STOCK Act of 2012 (Public Law 112–105) or any other applicable Federal law governing insider trading, conflicts of interest, or financial disclosure.
This Act shall be construed in conjunction with, and not in derogation of, chapter 131 of title 5, United States Code, and the financial disclosure requirements applicable to Federal candidates.

section.text: This Act shall take effect on the date that is 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act and shall apply to any individual who files for Federal office on or after such effective date.
